headline: Sykes averages 104 on debut to set up Humphries tie
standfirst: Tom Sykes beat Krzysztof Ratajski 5-1 to win Group J in Wolverhampton and says he believes he can go far in a televised major.
body: Tom Sykes finished top of Group J at the Grand Slam of Darts on his debut, beating Krzysztof Ratajski 5-1 in Wolverhampton with an average of 104.30. The win sends him into a last-16 meeting with Luke Humphries on Thursday.

Ratajski averaged 101.96 but won only one leg. Sykes converted five of his seven darts at double, broke in the opening leg with a two-dart 68 and followed it with a 130 checkout for a 2-0 lead. He went 4-1 ahead after a 42 finish and a missed double from his opponent.

He then had a dart at double 14 for a 145 checkout to win the match. Ratajski missed his attempt, and Sykes finished the job first time. "I really, really fancied the 145," he told Dartsnews afterwards, saying an adrenaline rush had got to him on the double.

Sykes had also beaten Luke Woodhouse, the seeded player in the group, on the opening day. He described that match as tense, and said his doubles settling down in the second game was the difference. According to Dartsnews, he believes that once they start going in he can average 102 or 103 and win games against the best players.

Asked whether he could win a televised tournament, he answered "100 per cent", pointing to his scoring power. He earned his first PDC Tour Card at UK Q School in January and said he found the adjustment fairly easy because he had already played on the ProTour.
Humphries, who also advanced from the group stage, is the next test for Sykes, with the second half of the last 16 played on Thursday.

sources.title: “I’ve got the scoring game to play against anybody” - Tom Sykes backs himself to win a TV major as 104 average sets up Luke Humphries clash at Grand Slam of Darts
